title: Tech Note: Launching Multiple Instances of 4D Server Automatically on Macintosh and Windows
author: Fred Johnson

historical_commentary.text: This note documents how to auto-launch multiple 4D Server instances on classic Mac OS (via ResEdit Creator-code tricks and Startup Items aliases) and Windows 95/NT (via per-instance .bat files and Startup folder shortcuts), plus how to distinguish instances on TCP/IP or IPX/SPX using port numbers since those protocols lacked ADSP's multi-server broadcast capability. Virtually every specific mechanism described is obsolete: ResEdit and classic Mac OS Creator codes vanished with Mac OS X, IPX/SPX networking disappeared entirely, and modern OS service managers (launchd, Windows Services) replace hand-built Startup Items/.bat approaches. The underlying goal — running multiple named/addressable server instances on one host — remains a standard IT concept, now solved with OS-native service management and standard TCP port binding.
related_updates: ResEdit and classic Mac OS resource/Creator-code editing were discontinued along with classic Mac OS itself (superseded by Mac OS X in 2001)
IPX/SPX networking was phased out industry-wide in favor of TCP/IP by the early 2000s
AppleTalk networking protocol was discontinued by Apple in the 2000s

Modern operating systems use dedicated service managers (e.g. launchd, Windows Services) rather than Startup Items aliases or .bat files in a Startup folder for auto-launching background server processes
